title: Interaction Gateway PRD — scope wedges, behavioral constraints, and launch safeguards
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: This PRD defines a lightweight Interaction Gateway that allows a single client request to route, fan-out, or compose calls across chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank endpoints under a consistent behavioral contract. The Gateway is intended to reduce client-side orchestration, centralize policy (timeouts, graded fallbacks, cost caps), and provide a single launch path for a set of use-cases (search+rerank, assistant + retrieval, scoring pipelines). This document captures scope wedges for an incremental launch, clarifies acceptance criteria per surface, and lays out operational launch safeguards.
goals: Provide a single endpoint that can express multi-step interaction patterns (retrieve -> rerank -> generate) without client orchestration
Ensure predictable cost and latency via per-request budget and graded fallbacks
Ship with eval-driven behavioral contracts so outputs remain within quality bounds for each composed flow
Minimize platform changes for hosted: avoid new long-lived state; leverage existing hosted model catalog and routing
out_of_scope: Full orchestration DSL (no workflow engine) — the gateway exposes a declarative composition spec limited to linear step sequences
Long-running background jobs or async job queues (no streaming persistence beyond existing KV caching)
Dedicated capacity variant and private VPC deployment for initial launch
required_behaviors: Chat step: preserves system/user messages order and enforces max token limit per step
Completion step: supports temperature/stop tokens and deterministic seed when requested
Embeddings step: returns vectors in the platform canonical format with stable dimensionality and deterministic hashing for identical input
Rerank step: accepts candidate list, returns stable ranking scores and top-k ordered ids; supports tie-breaking policy

Composition semantics: steps execute sequentially; later steps can reference prior step outputs via position-based refs; failure in a non-critical step can trigger a graded fallback (e.g., use sparse match if embeddings fail)
Cost guards: per-request token spend cap and per-step soft and hard timeouts with observable reason codes
Deterministic degrade: when fallback occurs, the gateway must annotate response with degrade_reason and degrade_level
acceptance_criteria: API contract: OpenAPI spec published and SDKs updated with gateway helper; acceptance tests validate schema for composition spec
Behavioral tests: golden prompt suite (1000 prompts) passes eval thresholds for end-to-end flows: retrieval+rerank+generate F1/ROUGE/quality delta within defined limits
Latency: 95th percentile end-to-end latency <= 1.2s for simple compose (embedding+p95 + rerank+p95 + generate+p95) under baseline canary load
Cost: average token spend per composed request within 15% of simulated client-side orchestration baseline
Fallbacks: in simulated failure modes (model OOM, regional outage), gateway performs graded fallback and total requests with degrade_level > 0 must be <= 2% in steady state
Observability: per-request traces include step timings, model variant, and cost breakdown; dashboards for per-step error rates are available
SLOs: availability >= 99.9% for the gateway endpoint in the hosted environment during business hours
Security: SAML/OAuth token passthrough verified for tenant contexts; KMS integration validated for any ephemeral keys used
Compatibility: existing single-surface clients (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank) must be unaffected by default routing; gateway is opt-in via a new route
telemetry_and_slos: End-to-end p95 latency target for simple two-step flows: <= 1200ms
Per-step error rate target: <0.5% p50, <1.5% p95
Fallback rate alert if >1% sustained over 15m
Token cost variance: alert if mean token spend deviates >20% vs baseline
rollout_checklist: Feature flag gate implemented (control at tenant level)
Canary: 0.5% of traffic routed to gateway within first 24h; verify basic metrics
Scale canary to 5% for 48h; run golden prompt suite against canary traffic
Open early access to 10 strategic accounts with support and SLA waiver
Gradual rollout to all tenants by traffic slicing (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with automated rollback on specified alerts
Operational runbook published (runbooks/interaction-gateway-runbook.md) and on-call training completed
Dashboard: per-step cost, per-step latency, degrade_reason distribution, tenant-level fallback rates
Cutover: SDK release notes and migration guide published; mark gateway as opt-in for first release
risk_mitigation: Risk: runaway cost from mis-specified compositions — Mitigation: enforce per-request hard token cap and sandboxed cost estimator
Risk: quality regression when composing models — Mitigation: evals gating and canary traffic with golden prompts and human review
Risk: third-party model instability — Mitigation: default fallback model variants and immediate downgrade policy
Risk: multi-tenant leakage via shared cache — Mitigation: tenant-scoped KV cache and strict isolation checks in QA
QA_plan: Unit tests for parser and composition validator (schema and ref resolution)
Integration tests that spin up a mini-hosted stack to validate routing, cost accounting, and degrade annotations
End-to-end regression harness running the golden prompt suite across multiple model families
Chaos tests injecting step failures and network partitions to confirm graded fallbacks and runbook actions
Security pen-test focused on token passthrough and tenant isolation for cache and tracing headers
decisions: Gateway will be opt-in (new /v1/interaction route) to prevent breaking existing clients
Composition language limited to linear sequences and positional refs (no branching, loops) for v1
Per-request hard token cap set to 8000 tokens (configurable by tenant in future)
Fallback policy levels: 0 (none), 1 (best-effort degrade), 2 (serve cached/spare-model result)
